claim: Which lipid a legend colour means in the viability dose panels
locus_A: Figure S3 legend (SI p.39): right column reads 7, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14
locus_B: Figure S4 legend (SI p.40): right column reads 7, 9, 11, 13, 12, 14 -- positions 4 and 5 SWAPPED
measurement: Swatches sampled from each panel's own raster. S3's 'Lipid 13' swatch is RGB (127,4,127); S4's 'Lipid 12' swatch is RGB (128,0,129). EUCLIDEAN DISTANCE 4.58, below heatmap.MAX_DIST (~5). The two panels also differ on Lipid 14: S3 (67,6,91) dark purple vs S4 (0,0,128) navy, distance 76.
what_we_emitted: Figure S4 values only, each bar assigned by heatmap.match against S4's OWN swatches. Nothing was matched across panels.
why: THE SAME COLOUR IS LIPID 13 IN ONE PANEL AND LIPID 12 IN THE OTHER, and the difference is small enough that a cross-panel colour match would return a confident wrong answer without ever tripping the max-distance guard that exists to catch exactly this. Independently corroborated by the drawn bar ORDER: in S4's 0.06 group the plotted sequence is ...11, 13, 12, 14, i.e. it follows S4's legend and not S3's.
status: OPEN -- unresolvable from the SI; only the authors know which panel's labelling is right

locus_B: Figures S3 and S4 (SI p.39-40) legends list twelve: Lipid 8 and Lipid 10 are ABSENT from both

claim: Which lipids the toxicology tables cover
locus_A: Caption of Table S1 and of Table S2 (SI p.47, p.48), both: 'LNPs based on the different lipids (2, 6, 8 and 10)'
locus_B: Body of both tables carries Lipid 13 rows at 2 h and 24 h in addition to 2, 6, 8 and 10
measurement: pdfplumber.find_tables() returns 12x14 and 12x17; 11 data rows each = UT + 5 lipids x 2 timepoints. The caption names 4 lipids, the body has 5.
what_we_emitted: All 11 rows of each table, with the lipid taken from the ROW LABEL, not the caption.
why: The row label is the primary record of what was measured; the caption is a summary of it. A caption that undercounts its own table is a transcription slip, not evidence that the Lipid 13 rows are spurious.
retired_by: Row labels in the extracted table

claim: Figures S2 and S4 report the same experiment and must agree
locus_A: Figure S2 (p.38): 'LNPs containing NC-siRNA at 0.06 uM for 72hrs ... XTT'
locus_B: Figure S4 (p.40), 0.06 uM group: 'LNPs containing siNC at different doses for 72hrs ... XTT'
measurement: 12 shared lipids digitised independently in both panels, each from its own 7-tick calibration. EIGHT agree to within 0.3% (ratios 0.9971-1.0034). FOUR do not: Lipid 2 x0.943, Lipid 3 x1.313 (93.75% vs 123.10%, a 29.35 pp gap), Lipid 4 x1.044, Lipid 5 x1.110. Mean ratio 1.0345, sd 0.0918. Spearman rank correlation across the 12 is only 0.48.
what_we_emitted: Both panels' values, separately, each tagged with its own source. No merge, no average.
why: That eight of twelve match to three decimal places proves the digitisation is sound AND that the two panels largely share one underlying dataset. Against that baseline the four that differ cannot be rounding or replication noise. Confirmed visually: Lipid 3 really is the tallest bar in S4's 0.06 group.
status: OPEN -- the two panels disagree about four lipids and only the authors can say which is right

claim: Lipid 4 contains two C=C double bonds
locus_A: Lipid 4's own 1H NMR (SI p.12) reports 4H + 4H in the olefinic window = 8 vinyl H, i.e. FOUR C=C
locus_B: Both of Lipid 4's immediate precursors report 4 vinyl H: the Boc-hydrazine (ESI-MS 609 [M+1]+, SI p.11) and the free hydrazine (ESI-MS 509.5 [M+1]+, SI p.11)
measurement: Mass settles it. Di((Z)-non-2-en-1-yl) backbone with 2 C=C gives C36H67N3O5, monoisotopic [M+H]+ 622.515 against the found 622.6 (dev +0.085 Da). Four C=C would be C36H63N3O5, [M+H]+ 618.48 -- 4.1 Da away and outside any reading of a low-resolution ESI value.
why: Mass cannot see connectivity but it CAN see degrees of unsaturation. Two independent precursor NMRs and the lipid's own mass all say two; only the final NMR's olefinic integral says four, and it is the only one of the four that is a transcription rather than a measurement of the final compound.
status: RESOLVED -- structure stands; the printed integral is wrong

measurement: The paper disagrees with ITSELF by 2.37 Da on one compound, on one line. Our enumerated C54H106N2O6 has monoisotopic M 878.805 ([M+H]+ 879.812, dev +0.308 from the printed 880.12) and average M 879.45. The singly-charged ion is consistent with the structure; the doubly-charged one is not, on either convention.
what_we_emitted: C54H106N2O6, anchored on the singly-charged ion.
why: No structure of ours takes part in the comparison between two numbers printed on the same line, so this is the paper against itself. The other three doubly-charged ions in the SI (Lipid 2, 9, 12) agree with their own structures to 0.03, 0.16 and 0.33 Da, so the method is normally sound and this one value is the outlier.
status: OPEN -- unresolvable; flagged on the row

locus_B: SI p.2, author manuscript header: '... for RNAi Delivery to Leukocytes'

claim: The identity of the silyl protecting group in the Lipid 14 route
locus_B: Same paragraph's reagent: 'tert-butyldiphenylsilylchloride (TBDPS-Cl)'; the drawn intermediate is labelled TBDPSO; the product NMR (p.34) shows 7.70-7.65 (4H, m) and 7.46-7.34 (6H, m), i.e. ten aromatic H
measurement: Ten aromatic protons are two phenyl rings. TBS has none. The reagent, the scheme label and the NMR all say TBDPS against a heading that says TBS.
what_we_emitted: Nothing -- this is an intermediate, not an emitted structure. Lipid 14 carries no silicon.
why: Recorded because a reader reconstructing the route from headings alone would build the wrong intermediate, and because it is the same class as C-09: a name in this SI is less reliable than the measurement beside it.
status: RESOLVED -- cosmetic; no emitted structure affected

claim: The identity of the oxo acid in the Lipid 12 route
locus_A: SI p.30: 'The above 7-oxoheptanoic acid (0.26 g, 2.00 mmol)'
locus_B: The compound actually prepared two paragraphs earlier is 6-hydroxyhexanoic acid (from caprolactone) oxidised by IBX, and the product is named '(Z)-non-3-en-1-yl 6-oxohexanoate'
measurement: The product's ESI-MS is 277 ([M+Na]+). C15H26O3 (the hexanoate) has monoisotopic M 254.188, [M+Na]+ 277.177 -- dev 0.18 Da. The heptanoate C16H28O3 would give [M+Na]+ 291.19, 14 Da away.
what_we_emitted: The hexanoate; Lipid 12 is built on a C6 diacid-derived arm.
why: Mass discriminates cleanly here because the two candidates differ by a whole CH2.

claim: Table S1 Lipid 10 / 2 h haematocrit standard deviation
locus_B: Every other SD in the table is a single decimal number
measurement: '0.2.3' is not a number. float() rejects it; a character-class regex accepts it, which is how it was nearly stored as a real SD.
what_we_emitted: The mean 51.300 is NOT emitted as a parsed value either: the whole cell is carried as value_raw_text with extraction_note 'UNPARSED: not a number'.
why: Left unrepaired on purpose. '0.23', '0.2' and '2.3' are all plausible readings and the SI gives no way to choose; guessing one would put a fabricated precision into a toxicology table.

claim: Table S1 Lipid 8 / 2 h platelet standard deviation
locus_B: The ten other platelet SDs in the same column run 72.42 to 393.2, i.e. 400x to 2000x larger
measurement: An SD of 0.18 on a platelet count of 1020 across n mice is not a measurement any CBC analyser produces; the adjacent haematocrit cell in the SAME ROW also ends in 0.18, which is the signature of a copy down or across a spreadsheet.
what_we_emitted: The printed value, verbatim, with this contradiction row attached.
why: Flagged rather than corrected. The suspected source (the neighbouring cell) is a hypothesis about a spreadsheet, not a reading of the paper, and C-10 is the same class: an implausible number is not a licence to invent a plausible one.

claim: Whether the SI's ESI-MS values are monoisotopic or average masses
locus_A: Lipids 1, 2, 4 and 13 sit closest to monoisotopic [M+H]+ (dev -0.030 to +0.308 Da)
locus_B: Lipids 6, 7, 8, 9, 12 and 14 sit closest to AVERAGE [M+H]+ (dev -0.006 to -0.212 Da); lipids 3, 5, 10 and 11 are printed as bare integers and cannot discriminate
measurement: All 14 enumerated formulae agree with their printed m/z to within 0.76 Da on the best of the three interpretations, so the FORMULA is confirmed for every lipid; the convention is not consistent within the SI.
what_we_emitted: All 14 structures; the QC records the per-lipid deviation under all three interpretations rather than picking one.
why: THE SI PRINTS NO 'Calc.' COLUMN ANYWHERE. There is no stated calculated mass to compare against, only found m/z from a low-resolution instrument, so which theoretical mass each value means had to be determined rather than read. Quoting a single convention for this paper would be inventing a precision the SI does not have.
status: RESOLVED -- report all three; claim formula only
